### 1. mutation-write-paths-drop-original-encoding

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | Confirmed live at all four cited anchors (2026-08-06 re-read). Root cause: three mutation apply paths write pre-mutation Roslyn `SourceText`/XML content back to disk through APIs that default to UTF-8-no-BOM, discarding the file's original encoding: (1) `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/EditService.cs:715` — `PersistDocumentTextToDiskAsync` calls `(await document.GetTextAsync(ct)).ToString()` (`EditService.cs:714`), converting the `SourceText` to a bare `string` and throwing away `SourceText.Encoding` *before* handing it to `AtomicFileWriter.WriteAllTextAsync(document.FilePath, text, ct)` (`EditService.cs:715`), which is `apply_text_edit`'s write path (traced via `ApplyTextEditsAsync` → `PersistDocumentTextToDiskAsync` call at `EditService.cs:638`). (2) `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ProjectMutationService.cs:565` calls the same `AtomicFileWriter.WriteAllTextAsync(projectFilePath, updatedContent, ct)` with no encoding, even though the method already reads the pre-apply bytes one line earlier for undo purposes (`ProjectMutationService.cs:554-558`) — the bytes are read but never used to detect encoding. (3) `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/EditorConfigService.cs:375` calls `File.WriteAllLines(editorconfigPath, lines)` (no `Encoding` overload argument) inside `SetOptionAsync`, which likewise already has the pre-apply bytes in scope as `existingBytes` (`EditorConfigService.cs:345`) but never converts them to an `Encoding`. The shared write primitive itself, `AtomicFileWriter.WriteAllTextAsync` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/CompositeApplyOrchestrator.cs:131-137`), forwards to `File.WriteAllTextAsync(tmp, content, ct)` with no `Encoding` parameter at all — .NET's parameterless-encoding overload is UTF-8-no-BOM by definition, so every caller of this shared helper is structurally incapable of preserving a source BOM/UTF-16 file today. This is a genuine spin-off, not a duplicate: the sibling `direct-mutation-undo-byte-fidelity` initiative (PR #1144) fixed the **undo/restore** half by capturing `FileSnapshotDto.OriginalBytes` and restoring via `AtomicFileWriter.WriteAllBytesAsync` (`UndoService.cs:363-368`) when a byte snapshot exists — the **forward apply** half addressed here is untouched by that fix. Not a Rule-1 bundle candidate: `bundleCandidatePeers` was empty. |
| Approach | Root-cause fix: thread the pre-mutation file's detected `Encoding` through each write instead of relying on parameterless defaults, reusing the existing internal BOM-detection helper rather than inventing a new one (stays within the 4-file cap). (1) `CompositeApplyOrchestrator.cs`: add an optional trailing `Encoding? encoding = null` parameter to `AtomicFileWriter.WriteAllTextAsync` (appended AFTER the existing `ILogger? logger = null` parameter, not inserted before it, so the 3 positional callers in `UndoService.cs` and the composite-mutation call at `CompositeApplyOrchestrator.cs:80` — which pass `logger` positionally — keep compiling unchanged); when non-null, the inner `writeTempAsync` lambda calls `File.WriteAllTextAsync(tmp, content, encoding, ct)` instead of the encoding-less overload. (2) `EditService.cs:701-715`: keep the `SourceText` object returned by `document.GetTextAsync(ct)` instead of collapsing it to `string` immediately; pass `text: sourceText.ToString()`, `encoding: sourceText.Encoding ?? new UTF8Encoding(encoderShouldEmitUTF8Identifier: false)` to `AtomicFileWriter.WriteAllTextAsync` via the new named `encoding:` parameter — `SourceText.Encoding` already carries the encoding Roslyn detected when the document was loaded, so this needs no new byte re-read. (3) `ProjectMutationService.cs:553-565`: reuse `RoslynMcp.Roslyn.Helpers.CsprojSemanticEquality.CreateSnapshot(byte[])` (`CsprojSemanticEquality.cs:264-277` — internal, same assembly, no new `using` beyond the existing `RoslynMcp.Roslyn.Helpers` namespace already referenced elsewhere in the assembly) against the `preApplySnapshot`'s pre-apply bytes already read at `ProjectMutationService.cs:557` to get `.TextEncoding`; when the file doesn't yet exist, fall back to `new UTF8Encoding(encoderShouldEmitUTF8Identifier: false)` (current behavior, correct for new files). Pass the result to `AtomicFileWriter.WriteAllTextAsync(..., encoding: writeEncoding)`. (4) `EditorConfigService.cs:345,375`: same `CsprojSemanticEquality.CreateSnapshot(existingBytes)` reuse against the already-in-scope `existingBytes` local, then call `File.WriteAllLines(editorconfigPath, lines, writeEncoding)` — the BCL overload that accepts an explicit `Encoding` — using the detected encoding (or the UTF8-no-BOM default when `created` is true / no prior file). `CsprojSemanticEquality.CreateSnapshot` is a generic BOM/encoding detector (`StreamReader` with `detectEncodingFromByteOrderMarks: true`) despite its "Csproj"-scoped name; reusing it for a non-csproj `.editorconfig` file is a deliberate scope-cap tradeoff flagged in Risks, not a rename — a follow-up rename to a neutrally-named helper is left for later since it's non-blocking. |
| Scope | **4 production files** (at Rule 3's cap; no exemption needed): `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/CompositeApplyOrchestrator.cs` (signature-only change to `AtomicFileWriter.WriteAllTextAsync`, purely additive/optional param — non-breaking), `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/EditService.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/ProjectMutationService.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/EditorConfigService.cs`. **3 test files extended** (Rule 4, within cap): `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ApplyTextEditVerifyTests.cs`, `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/ProjectMutationIntegrationTests.cs`, `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/EditorConfigServiceTests.cs` — each gets a `[DataRow(false)][DataRow(true)]`-style `useUtf16` test method mirroring the existing byte-fidelity fixture pattern at `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/UndoFileOperationsTests.cs:75-119` (`Encoding.GetPreamble().Concat(Encoding.GetBytes(content))` fixture construction, `CollectionAssert.AreEqual` on post-apply bytes). ### 2. lru-eviction-concurrent-reader-safety-overstated

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | Confirmed live. `WorkspaceManager.cs:248-249` LRU scan filters candidates on `s.LoadLock.CurrentCount > 0` — `LoadLock` is acquired/released only inside `LoadIntoSessionAsync` (`WorkspaceManager.cs:818,967`), i.e. only during an active `workspace_load`/reload. Ordinary reads/writes go through `WorkspaceExecutionGate`'s separate per-workspace `AsyncReaderWriterLockRegistry` (`WorkspaceExecutionGate.cs:51`, `ReaderLockAsync`/`WriterLockAsync` at `WorkspaceExecutionGate.cs:218,225`) — the LRU scan never consults it. `WorkspaceManager.Close()` (`WorkspaceManager.cs:381-401`) is called directly from the LRU branch of `LoadAsync` (`WorkspaceManager.cs:260`) and immediately does `_sessions.TryRemove` + `session.Dispose()` with zero coordination against the gate. Contrast with the CORRECT pattern already in this codebase: `workspace_close` (`WorkspaceTools.cs:137-163`) and `workspace_reload` (`WorkspaceTools.cs:101-108`) both nest `gate.RunWriteAsync(workspaceId, ...)` inside `gate.RunLoadGateAsync(...)` specifically so in-flight readers on that workspace complete before `Close()`/`ReloadAsync` runs — the LRU eviction path is the ONE lifecycle transition that skips this pattern. `ToolDispatch.cs:329-341`'s XML remarks state '...an in-flight workspace is never yanked out from under a concurrent caller' — this is true only for the load path; it overstates the actual guarantee for readers/writers. Additional re-derived finding (Directive #5, not in the original item): the concrete failure mode is inconsistent across call sites. `WorkspaceManager.GetCurrentSolution` (`WorkspaceManager.cs:637-672`) defensively catches `ObjectDisposedException` on `workspace.CurrentSolution` and translates it to a retryable `StaleWorkspaceTransitionException`; `WorkspaceManager.GetProject` (`WorkspaceManager.cs:687-688`) reads `session.Workspace?.CurrentSolution` with NO such catch, so a reader mid-flight through that path gets a raw, unhandled `ObjectDisposedException` — the item's evidence cites 'ObjectDisposedException' generically; the precise mechanism is call-site-dependent. |
| Approach | Root-cause fix chosen: correct the two overstated safety comments (Acceptance's first OR-branch, option 2) rather than attempt the full architectural fix, because the full fix requires `WorkspaceManager.LoadAsync`'s eviction step to acquire the evicted candidate's write lock via `IWorkspaceExecutionGate.RunWriteAsync` before calling `Close()` — but `WorkspaceExecutionGate`'s constructor already takes `IWorkspaceManager`, so injecting `IWorkspaceExecutionGate` into `WorkspaceManager` is a direct constructor-level DI cycle. The only clean real fix is moving eviction-candidate execution (not just selection) out of `WorkspaceManager.LoadAsync` into the `WorkspaceTools`/Gate layer where both already coexist without a cycle — genuine surgery on the load retry-loop (`WorkspaceManager.cs:240-292`, the `goto slotAcquired`/`goto strictError` control flow) that is L-sized and out of scope for this M row; the item's own Acceptance criteria explicitly sanctions the documentation+pin path as a complete resolution. 1) `WorkspaceManager.cs:244-251` — rewrite the eviction-scan comment: remove the parenthetical '(i.e. are actively being loaded or read)' and state precisely that the `LoadLock.CurrentCount > 0` filter only excludes workspaces mid-`LoadIntoSessionAsync`; a workspace with in-flight reads/writes via `WorkspaceExecutionGate` is NOT excluded and can be disposed concurrently. 2) `ToolDispatch.cs:327-341` — rewrite the XML remarks paragraph containing 'an in-flight workspace is never yanked out from under a concurrent caller' to state the true guarantee: LRU eviction protects only the load path; a workspace with in-flight reads/writes through `WorkspaceExecutionGate` can still be evicted and disposed mid-operation, surfacing as `ObjectDisposedException` (`GetProject`-style paths) or `StaleWorkspaceTransitionException` (`GetCurrentSolution`-style paths) to the unlucky caller. 3) `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/WorkspaceCapLruEvictionTests.cs` — add one characterization test that wires a real `WorkspaceExecutionGate` + `WorkspaceManager` pair (mirroring production DI), starts a `gate.RunReadAsync` on workspace1 gated by a `TaskCompletionSource` so the reader lock is held, triggers an `EvictPolicy.Lru` load of workspace2 from the test thread (invoking `manager.Close(workspace1Id)` directly, bypassing the gate — the exact bug), releases the TCS, and asserts the blocked read observes the disposed `MSBuildWorkspace` (via `manager.GetProject(workspace1Id, ...)`, which has no defensive catch, expecting `ObjectDisposedException`). Mirror the existing test file's `CreateManager` helper and `[DoNotParallelize]` class attribute. |
| Scope | Production files (2): `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/WorkspaceManager.cs` (comment-only edit, ~lines 244-251), `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ToolDispatch.cs` (XML-doc-only edit, ~lines 327-341). Test files (1, extended not new): `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/WorkspaceCapLruEvictionTests.cs` (add one `[TestMethod]`). No Rule 3 exemption needed — well under the 4-file cap. |

### 3. validate-workspace-diagnostic-harvest-reconcile

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | `WorkspaceValidationService.ValidateInternalAsync` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/WorkspaceValidationService.cs:243-248`) builds `allErrors` by concatenating `compile.Diagnostics` (compile_check's own harvest, `ErrorCount`-backed) with `diagResult.CompilerDiagnostics` AND `diagResult.AnalyzerDiagnostics` (the second, independent `project_diagnostics` harvest). `WorkspaceValidationDto.ErrorCount` (`WorkspaceValidationService.cs:277`) is `allErrors.Length`. PR #1140 (`validate-workspace-compiler-category-status-mismatch`) fixed `ComputeOverallStatus` (`WorkspaceValidationService.cs:539-554`) so a `Category=="Compiler"` row present ONLY in the merged list — i.e. surfaced by `diagResult.CompilerDiagnostics` while `compile.ErrorCount==0` — degrades to `"analyzer-error"` instead of the pre-fix `"compile-error"`. That relabeled the VERDICT string only: the row still enters `allErrors`/`ErrorCount`, so the retro's green-build repro (0 compile errors, 0 warnings, 35/35 tests green) still returns `overallStatus:"analyzer-error"` / `errorCount:1` instead of `"clean"` / `0`. Root cause of the harvest disagreement: `diagResult.CompilerDiagnostics` sources from `DiagnosticService.CollectProjectDiagnosticsAsync` (`DiagnosticService.cs:168-215`) via `compilation.GetDiagnostics(ct)` on a compilation obtained through `_compilationCache.GetCompilationAsync` (`DiagnosticService.cs:180`, the version-keyed `CompilationCache`), while `CompileCheckService.CollectDiagnosticsAsync` (`CompileCheckService.cs:128-151`) obtains its compilation via a direct `project.GetCompilationAsync(ct)` call (`CompileCheckService.cs:140`), bypassing `ICompilationCache` entirely. `ValidateInternalAsync` calls the two services sequentially (`compile` stage at `:227-233`, then `diagResult` stage at `:237-242`) against `IWorkspaceManager` reads taken independently at each stage — `CompilationCache.GetCompilationAsync`'s own doc comment (`CompilationCache.cs:66-70`) documents a "lost racer" window where a concurrent caller's task can install a different entry than the one a given reader observes, so the two harvests are not guaranteed to see identical compilation state even within one `ValidateAsync` call. `WorkspaceValidationService`'s existing doc comment (`:526-538`) already names this mechanism; PR #1140 fixed only the derived verdict string. Fix path chosen: the stage-2 doc comment (`:235-236`) states the harvest's only intentional purpose is "to add CA*/IDE* errors (compile_check is compiler-only)" — `diagResult.CompilerDiagnostics` was never meant to be an independent arbiter of compiler errors, `compile.Diagnostics`/`compile.ErrorCount` already is. Gating `diagResult.CompilerDiagnostics` on `compile.ErrorCount > 0` (the same corroboration signal `ComputeOverallStatus` already trusts) extends that trust rule from the verdict to the count/list, and doubles as the "test pinning the reconciliation rule" the row's Acceptance bullet 2 allows as an alternative to eliminating the underlying cache race. No Rule-1 bundling — `bundleCandidatePeers` was empty. |
| Approach | Extract the `allErrors` computation out of `ValidateInternalAsync` (`WorkspaceValidationService.cs:243-248`) into a new `internal static DiagnosticDto[] MergeErrorDiagnostics(CompileCheckDto compile, DiagnosticsResultDto diagResult)` on `WorkspaceValidationService` — mirrors the existing `internal static ComputeOverallStatus` pattern (`:539`) so it is independently unit-testable without a real workspace fixture. Inside, gate `diagResult.CompilerDiagnostics` on `compile.ErrorCount > 0`: only merge those rows when the authoritative compile pass corroborates at least one real compiler error; when `compile.ErrorCount == 0` they contribute nothing to the returned array. `diagResult.AnalyzerDiagnostics` stays unconditional (unchanged) — those are the CA*/IDE* errors `compile_check` genuinely cannot see. Update `ValidateInternalAsync` (`:254` area) to call `MergeErrorDiagnostics(compile, diagResult)` in place of the inline LINQ chain. Add a doc comment on the new method citing `validate-workspace-diagnostic-harvest-reconcile` and the corroboration rule, matching the file's existing comment style (e.g. the `validate-workspace-compiler-category-status-mismatch` block at `:526-538`). No other files change — `ComputeOverallStatus`'s signature and callers are untouched. |
| Scope | Production files (1): `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/WorkspaceValidationService.cs` (extract `MergeErrorDiagnostics`, gate the merge, update the call site). Test files (1, extended): `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/WorkspaceValidationOverallStatusTests.cs` (new `[TestMethod]`s targeting `MergeErrorDiagnostics` directly, alongside the existing `ComputeOverallStatus` tests). No new files, no structural-unit or tool-surface-only exemption needed — plain fix/refactor within the 4-file Rule-3 cap. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |

### 10. compilation-cache-adoption-read-side

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | `CompilationCache.GetCompilationAsync` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/CompilationCache.cs:56-80`) and `GetCompilationWithAnalyzersAsync`/`BuildCompilationWithAnalyzersAsync` (`:82-124`) each install one shared `Task` per `(workspaceId, ProjectId)` in a `ConcurrentDictionary`, but that shared task is started with the FIRST caller's `CancellationToken` (line 71 `project.GetCompilationAsync(ct)`; line 92 `BuildCompilationWithAnalyzersAsync(workspaceId, project, ct)`, which itself threads `ct` into a nested `GetCompilationAsync` call at line 105). If that first caller cancels, the shared `Task` transitions to `Canceled` and stays installed in the dictionary — every later caller hitting the same key at the unchanged workspace version does `TryGetValue` → returns the SAME canceled task, so `await`ing it rethrows `OperationCanceledException` to a caller whose own token was never canceled. The entry is only replaced when `GetCurrentVersion` bumps (next apply/reload), so the poisoning window can span many unrelated tool calls. This is a real, already-documented, unresolved hazard (item doc `## Context`, flagged during the PR #1147 code-quality review as "amend, not a new row"); PR #1147 extended the exposure to 4 more services (`BuildService`, `FixAllService`, `BulkRefactoringService`, `CrossProjectRefactoringService`) on top of the ~10 already-adopted read-side services (batches 1/2/a), so roughly 14 production call sites are live-exposed today. Verified unfixed by reading the current file (lines 71/92 still pass `ct` straight through). Anchor re-derivation for the OTHER half of the row's next-deliverable ("split the remaining site groups") found the item doc's own site inventory materially stale: (a) the "Remaining group-a tail" (`ImpactSweepService`, `MutationAnalysisService`, `SymbolRelationshipService`) is WRONG — all three already route through `_compilationCache.GetCompilationAsync` (`ImpactSweepService.cs:138`, `MutationAnalysisService.cs:354`, `SymbolRelationshipService.cs:430`) and already have passing regression coverage (`CompilationCacheAdoptionTests.cs:232/336/355`), shipped in PR #1010 per `git log`; (b) `ScaffoldingService.*` (cited as "3 partial files / 7 sites") has ZERO `Compilation`/`GetCompilationAsync` references across all three partials today — that anchor never matched or was resolved without a doc update. Given that unreliability, this bounded batch does NOT attempt the remaining site-group split (group-b tail `InterfaceExtractionService:394/415`, group-c hazard `SymbolResolver`/`SymbolHandleSerializer`) — those need fresh per-site forked-vs-live classification, not a repeat of the stale inventory. |
| Approach | Single-file fix in `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/CompilationCache.cs`, mirrored across both cached methods: (1) start the underlying shared task with `CancellationToken.None` instead of the calling caller's `ct` — `GetCompilationAsync` line 71 (`project.GetCompilationAsync(...)`) and the `BuildCompilationWithAnalyzersAsync` task installed at line 92 — so the shared task's lifetime is decoupled from any single caller's token; (2) add a small per-caller observation wrapper using `Task<T>.WaitAsync(CancellationToken)` (.NET 6+, available on this repo's net10.0 TFM) so each caller still honors ITS OWN `ct` — the wrapper throws `OperationCanceledException` early on that caller's token without affecting the underlying shared task or other observers; (3) on the SHARED task itself completing canceled/faulted (not the per-caller wrapper timing out), evict the poisoned entry via `_compilations.TryRemove`/`_analyzerBound.TryRemove`, version-gated so a race against a newer `AddOrUpdate` winner is never evicted, so the next caller re-populates instead of replaying the same broken task until the workspace version bumps — this satisfies the item doc's explicit fix note verbatim ("detach cached tasks from any single caller's token ... evict entries whose task completed canceled/faulted instead of serving them"). `ICompilationCache` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Contracts/ICompilationCache.cs`) is untouched — no signature change, so none of the ~14 existing call sites need edits. |
| Scope | Production: 1 file — `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/CompilationCache.cs`. Test: 1 file (extended, not new) — `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/CompilationCacheAdoptionTests.cs`, adding a regression test matching the item doc's prescribed shape: caller A fetches with an already-canceled `CancellationToken` and observes `OperationCanceledException` from its own wrapper; caller B then fetches the SAME `(workspaceId, project)` at the unchanged version with `CancellationToken.None` and must receive a real `Compilation`, not a rethrown `OperationCanceledException` — proving the shared task survived caller A's cancellation. No Rule 3 exemption needed (well under the 4-file cap); this is deliberately a narrow bounded batch of the `size: L` row, not the full remaining scope. |
